problems.stem: A storyboard frame shows a branching simulation. Which research question turns that design feature into something a small study could actually answer?
options: Is the branching simulation engaging and visually appealing?
Does adding the branch point after the narration reduce the number of learners who skip the reader-action prompt, compared with the linear version?
Will learners enjoy the simulation more than a textbook?
Is the storyboard finished and ready to hand off?
problems.explanation: A study question names a design feature (the branch placement), an observable outcome (skipped prompts), and a comparison (linear version). The other options ask for opinions or completion, not evidence.

problems.stem: Which storyboard annotation is specific enough to become a testable study question rather than a vague design hope?
options: Signaling cue on frame 3 should cut the time learners spend hunting for the next action; check whether action-start time drops.
Add more color to the simulation.
problems.explanation: The strong annotation names the design element (signaling cue, frame 3), a mechanism (less hunting), and a measure (action-start time). The rest are reactions, not questions.

problems.stem: You ask an AI tool to help you turn a storyboard into a study question. What is the strongest bounded use of that help?
options: Have the AI write the entire research question and submit it unchanged.
Ask the AI to draft three candidate questions, then keep only the one that names a design element and a measurable learner action you can observe in this storyboard.
Avoid the AI because all study questions must be original.
Use the AI only to make the question sound more academic.
problems.explanation: Bounded use means the AI proposes options and you judge them against the storyboard's actual design features and observable outcomes. You stay responsible for the design-to-question link.

problems.stem: A peer writes the question, "Does my storyboard improve learning?" Why is this not yet usable, and what fixes it?
options: It is fine; learning improvement is the goal of every design.
It names no specific design feature and no observable measure, so no result could confirm or disconfirm it; bind it to one frame change and one learner action you can record.
It is too short; make it a full paragraph.
It needs a more polished storyboard before any question can be asked.
problems.explanation: An unfalsifiable question cannot guide revision. Tying it to a single design change and a single observable action makes the result interpretable.
